stories.title: Thar women challenge gender stereotypes as global campaign against violence begins
summary: The historic Palan Bazaar, adorned in orange to symbolise hope for a future free from violence against women and girls, became the venue for a dialogue on gender equality, women’s empowerment and the need to dismantle discriminatory social practices.

Speakers at the gathering stressed that discriminatory social norms not only deprived women of educational and employment opportunities but also perpetuated unequal power relations, discouraged survivors of violence from seeking justice and contributed to a culture of impunity.

They called for greater political commitment, effective implementation of laws, institutional accountability and collective efforts to ensure that women and girls could exercise their fundamental rights without fear of violence, discrimination or social exclusion.

stories.title: Sindh High Court restores dissolution of marriage provision in Christian divorce law
summary: KARACHI: The Sindh High Court on Wednesday revived a provision of the Divorce Act of 1869 that had been omitted in 1981, enabling Christian couples in the province to approach courts for dissolution of marriage on ordinary grounds.

Former military dictator Ziaul Haq had omitted Section 7 of the Divorce Act through an ordinance in July 1981, leaving Christian citizens with no ground to divorce their spouses except on charges of adultery.

The bench noted in its judgement that, apparently, the divorce law had recognised cruelty and desertion for two years or more as conduct sufficiently grave to warrant a decree of judicial separation, but not on their own as grounds for dissolution of the marriage.
